ledger.title: Rule 5h reads __builtin_expect(E, K) as E on a stated premise that E's truthiness survives its conversion to long
ledger.text: Registered by BUILTIN-EXPECT-NULL-TEST. The builtin's parameters are `long`: its value is `(long)E`, which has E's truthiness when E is a null or comparison test (int 0/1), or an integer no wider than `long` (LP64, the runs' targets); Clang rejects a pointer operand, but accepts a floating or `__int128` operand silently, where `(long)0.5` is 0 while `if (0.5)` is true. The token-level reading does not check the operand's type, so the premise is stated in rule 5h, not checked. DISCHARGE: read the operand's implicit conversion from the Clang AST (an integral cast from a type no wider than `long`, or a Boolean-valued operand) and refuse any other, with a fixture for a floating and a wider operand, Lean parity and a measurement (expected: no move; the census found no such operand).

ledger.title: A call-free connective or `?:` with a null leaf is accepted without refining the leaf, and accuses a leak no path has
ledger.text: Registered by BUILTIN-EXPECT-NULL-TEST. With a nullable owned `p = k_alloc(n)`, the bare `if (!p && n) { return; } if (!p) return; k_free(p);`, `return (p != 0) ? p : 0;` and `return p ? p : 0;` each report a leak (provisional Unsafe) although every path releases or returns `p` or holds nothing; the same tests under `__builtin_expect` are desugared by rule 5h and decided Safe (fixture in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/builtin_expect_null_test.rs). An older whole-condition route admits the call-free connective (and the pointer `?:` return) as neutral, keeping both edges without the null leaf's refinement. Not sized on the runs. DISCHARGE: census the corpus and current runs for such conditions; then lower a call-free connective or `?:` whose leaves include a null test through rule 5h's edges (or refuse it), with fixtures, Lean parity and a measurement showing no Safe move without a discharged obligation.

ledger.title: A null store after a release inside a loop does not reach the back edge, and the loop accuses a double release
ledger.text: Registered by BUILTIN-EXPECT-NULL-TEST. With a nullable owned `p = k_alloc(n)`, `while (p != 0) { k_free(p); p = 0; }` reports a double release, and `for (i = 0; i < 2; i++) { if (p != 0) { k_free(p); p = 0; } }` a double release and a leak, although after the store the test fails on every path; the straight-line `k_free(p); p = 0; if (p != 0) k_free(p);` is Safe. Wrapped and bare tests agree, so the wrapper is not involved. Not sized on the runs. DISCHARGE: census the runs for a release followed by a null store of the same name inside a loop; then carry the store's null fact across the back edge (or refuse the site), with fixtures, Lean parity and a measurement.
